Clamor

/KLAM-er/ - rhymes with hammer · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Clamor means a loud, continuous outcry or noise of many voices.

By the second week of the bread shortage, the clamor outside the bakery started before the ovens did.

Worked Example

When the reunion tour added a single hometown date, a clamor filled the box-office plaza by dawn — fans chanting for more shows, phones held up on speaker, somebody's air horn punctuating the demand — and it did not let up until a second night was posted.

Clamor is the exact noun because it means a loud, continuous outcry of many voices — and this noise wants something; it is demand you can hear. Racket is loudness with no message in it, and an uproar can be pure confusion; a clamor keeps asking until it is answered.

How Clamor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

uproar

uproar: a burst of loud confusion — no single demand required

outcry

outcry: public protest, as loud on paper as out loud

Antonyms

hush

hush: the sudden quiet that swallows a room

murmur

murmur: many voices kept low and soft

How Strong Is It? — murmur → clamor → bedlam

murmur vs. clamor

murmur vs. clamor: A murmur is sound at a simmer — voices low enough that no single word survives the trip across the room.

bedlam vs. clamor

bedlam vs. clamor: Bedlam goes further than clamor — a clamor is loud voices demanding something; bedlam is the room gone past demands into pure chaos.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — clam

Root — clam: to cry out (Latin clamare)

Suffix — -or

Suffix — -or: noun ending: the thing itself

Put it together

Put it together: Clam (to cry out) + -or (noun ending) = 'the crying-out itself.' Latin clamare is the ancestor of every English shout on record: claim began as crying out one's right, exclaim as crying out in surprise. A clamor is the raw noun — the shouting, bottled and labeled.

Use the root in a new word: exclaim

Use the root in a new word: exclaim: You exclaim when surprise cries out of you before you can shape it into a sentence.

Word Choice

neutral / journalistic

Clamor is noise with a demand inside it — crowds, markets, protests. For meaningless loudness, racket; for chaos, bedlam; and when one desperate voice does the asking, this unit's beseech is the verb, not clamor.
